items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names reveal intent (windowClauseToSQL, assertWindowName, WindowSpec). Every .window() has JSDoc with an example, and formatting matches the surrounding builder code. Single-letter names (m, s, q) appear only in tests.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Spec and validation logic lives in one window.ts (428 lines, under the 500 cap) and is reused by every dialect through windowClauseToSQL(windows). Each dialect adds only an optional field, a 3-line .window() and one chunk. No dead code or debug leftovers.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are validated at the boundaries: ntile/nthValue require positive integers, preceding/following reject negative or non-integer values, rows()/range() check from/to order (including unbounded edge cases), and window names are checked. Numbers are inlined, never bound. Non-numeric defaults are still bound as parameters.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: Purely additive: `export * from './window.ts'`, an optional `windows?: {name; spec}[]` on all five *SelectConfig, and the same `window(name, spec = {}): this` on pg/mysql/sqlite/singlestore/gel. windowSql is undefined when unused, so existing SQL is unchanged. All 566 existing (P2P) tests pass.
